audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 12, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Nathan's parable, property metaphors around women, direct confrontation, sexualized retaliation prophecy, confession without public repair, death of the child, grief, Bathsheba, Solomon/Jedidiah, Rabbah conquest, crown and spoil, and forced-labor/torture variants.

verses.restored: YHWH sent Nathan to David. He came and said, Two men were in one city, one rich and one poor.

familiar.text: And the LORD sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.

verses.restored: Rich man had very many flocks and herds.

familiar.text: The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds:

verses.restored: Poor man had nothing except one small ewe lamb he had bought. He sustained it, and it grew with him and his children. It ate from his portion, drank from his cup, lay in his bosom, and was like a daughter to him.

familiar.text: But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.

verses.restored: A traveler came to rich man. Rich man spared his own flock and herd and took poor man's ewe lamb, preparing it for traveler who came to him.

familiar.text: And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him; but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him.

verses.restored: David's anger burned greatly against man. He said to Nathan, As YHWH lives, man who did this is a son of death.

familiar.text: And David’s anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the LORD liveth, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die:

verses.restored: He shall repay lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he had no compassion.

familiar.text: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.

verses.restored: Nathan said to David, You are the man. Thus says YHWH, Divine of Israel: I anointed you king over Israel and rescued you from hand of Saul.

familiar.text: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;

verses.restored: I gave you house of your lord and women of your lord into your household, and I gave you house of Israel and Judah. If this were too little, I would add more and more.

familiar.text: And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things.

verses.restored: Why did you despise word of YHWH, doing evil in YHWH's eyes? Uriah the Hittite you struck with sword; his wife you took as your wife; him you killed by sword of children of Ammon.

familiar.text: Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.

verses.restored: Now sword shall not turn aside from your house, because you despised me and took wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.

familiar.text: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.

verses.restored: Thus says YHWH: Look, I am raising evil against you from your house. I will take your women before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, who will lie with your women before eyes of this sun.

familiar.text: Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.

verses.restored: You acted in secret, but this thing will be done before all Israel and before sun.

familiar.text: For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.

verses.restored: David said to Nathan, I have sinned against YHWH. Nathan said to David, YHWH also has passed over your sin; you shall not die.

familiar.text: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said unto David, The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.

verses.restored: Nevertheless, because by this deed you have utterly treated YHWH's enemies with contempt/caused contempt, the son born to you will surely die.

familiar.text: Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.

verses.restored: Nathan went to his house. YHWH struck child whom wife of Uriah bore to David, and he became gravely ill.

familiar.text: And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.

verses.restored: David sought Divine on behalf of child. David fasted, entered, and lay all night upon ground.

familiar.text: David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.

verses.restored: Elders of his house arose beside him to raise him from ground, but he was not willing and did not eat bread with them.

familiar.text: And the elders of his house arose, and went to him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.

verses.restored: On seventh day child died. Servants of David feared to tell him child was dead, because they said, Look, while child lived we spoke to him and he did not listen. How then can we say child is dead? He may harm himself/do evil.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead?

verses.restored: David saw his servants whispering and understood child was dead. David said to servants, Is child dead? They said, He is dead.

familiar.text: But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.

verses.restored: David arose from ground, washed, anointed himself, changed garments, came to house of YHWH, and bowed. He came to his house, asked, and they set bread before him, and he ate.

familiar.text: Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his apparel, and came into the house of the LORD, and worshipped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat.

verses.restored: His servants said to him, What is this thing you have done? For living child you fasted and wept; when child died, you arose and ate bread.

familiar.text: Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.

verses.restored: He said, While child lived, I fasted and wept, because I said, Who knows? YHWH may be gracious to me and child may live.

familiar.text: And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live?

verses.restored: Now he is dead. Why should I fast? Can I return him again? I am going to him, but he will not return to me.

familiar.text: But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.

verses.restored: David comforted Bathsheba his wife, came to her, and lay with her. She bore a son, and he called his name Solomon. YHWH loved him.

familiar.text: And David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the LORD loved him.

verses.restored: YHWH sent by hand of Nathan the prophet and called his name Jedidiah, for sake of YHWH.

familiar.text: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.

verses.restored: Joab fought against Rabbah of children of Ammon and captured royal city.

familiar.text: And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.

verses.restored: Joab sent messengers to David and said, I fought against Rabbah and captured city of waters.

familiar.text: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.

verses.restored: Now gather rest of people, camp against city, and capture it, lest I capture city and my name be called upon it.

familiar.text: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it: lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.

verses.restored: David gathered all people, went to Rabbah, fought against it, and captured it.

familiar.text: And David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.

verses.restored: He took crown of their king/Milcom from his head; its weight was a talent of gold with a precious stone. It was placed on David's head. He brought out spoil of city in very great abundance.

familiar.text: And he took their king’s crown from off his head, the weight whereof was a talent of gold with the precious stones: and it was set on David’s head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.

verses.restored: He brought out people who were in it and placed them under/at saws, iron picks, and iron axes, and made them pass through brickworks. Thus he did to all cities of children of Ammon. David and all people returned to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And he brought forth the people that were therein, and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brick-kiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.

translation_notes: Nathan confronts the king through a story that makes David recognize predatory taking. The parable's lamb is 'like a daughter'; Bathsheba herself is not Uriah's animal or property.
Verse 8 reflects ancient royal-household language that treats women as transferable. It must not be received as Divine endorsement of owning women.
Nathan names David as the killer of Uriah even though Ammonite weapons and Joab carried out the plan. Delegation does not dissolve command responsibility.

Verses 11-12 describe sexual violation of David's women as retaliation against David. Women may not be used as instruments of punishment, prophecy fulfillment, political messaging, or inherited consequences.
David's brief confession avoids his execution in the narrative, but forgiveness does not replace confession to survivors, truth-telling, reparations, loss of office, or institutional accountability.

The child's illness and death are morally intolerable as punishment for an adult's abuse. This text must never teach that children die because of parents' sexual sin or that infant death proves Divine anger.
Servants explicitly fear David may harm himself. His fasting and collapse require suicide-aware care rather than romantic spiritual heroism.
Bathsheba is again named as Uriah's wife in verse 15 and later as Bathsheba in verse 24. The birth of Solomon does not erase her abuse, Uriah, or the dead child.
Verse 31 is textually and translationally disputed between forced labor and torture. Neither reading makes conquest benign; both preserve coercion of Ammonite civilians.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Never use this chapter to blame a child for David's actions, reassure bereaved parents that death was punishment, or frame sexual violence against women as Divinely arranged justice. David's confession is not the end of accountability. Center Bathsheba, Uriah, the unnamed child, soldiers killed in the cover-up, and conquered Ammonite people.
